title: The Seed Swap
learning_objectives: Read a longer story independently and track two characters' plans
Explain a fair trade and why both sides were happy
parent_prompts: Let the child read alone. After: what did each child want? How did the swap make both happy? What went wrong at first?

pages.text: Lan had a jar of bean seeds, more than she could ever plant. Nia had a paper bag of sunflower seeds, big striped ones, more than she could ever plant either. "Swap?" said Lan. "Half for half," said Nia.
pages.illustration_brief: Lan (green) holding a jar of beans; Nia (purple) holding a paper bag of striped sunflower seeds; both grinning.
pages.audio_script: Lan had a jar of bean seeds, more than she could ever plant. Nia had a paper bag of sunflower seeds, big striped ones, more than she could ever plant either. Swap? said Lan. Half for half, said Nia.

vocabulary.definition: To give something and get something else back.

pages.image_alt: Lan holds a jar of bean seeds and Nia a paper bag of striped sunflower seeds, on a garden step.

pages.text: They counted on the step. Lan tipped out forty beans and pushed twenty across. Nia tipped out her bag: twelve sunflower seeds. Twelve! She pushed six across and looked at the pile of twenty beans. "That is not fair," she said.
pages.illustration_brief: Two piles on a doorstep: many small beans versus a few large sunflower seeds; Nia frowning.
pages.audio_script: They counted on the step. Lan tipped out forty beans and pushed twenty across. Nia tipped out her bag: twelve sunflower seeds. Twelve! She pushed six across and looked at the pile of twenty beans. That is not fair, she said.
pages.image_alt: Two piles of seeds on a step: a big pile of forty beans and a small pile of twelve striped sunflower seeds.

pages.text: "Twenty for six? It is not fair for me!" said Lan. They both stopped. Then they both laughed, because they had said the same thing about opposite piles.
pages.illustration_brief: Both girls pointing at each other's piles, mid-laugh.
pages.audio_script: Twenty for six? It is not fair for me! said Lan. They both stopped. Then they both laughed, because they had said the same thing about opposite piles.
pages.image_alt: Lan and Nia both with open mouths, each pointing at the other pile of seeds.

pages.text: "A bean makes a whole plant with lots of beans," said Lan. "A sunflower makes a whole flower with hundreds of seeds," said Nia. "So one is not worth one. But how many is one worth?"
pages.illustration_brief: Thought bubbles: a bean plant heavy with pods over Lan; a huge sunflower head over Nia.
pages.audio_script: A bean makes a whole plant with lots of beans, said Lan. A sunflower makes a whole flower with hundreds of seeds, said Nia. So one is not worth one. But how many is one worth?

vocabulary.definition: How much something is valued or what it can be traded for.
vocabulary.example: This old coin is worth a lot.

pages.image_alt: A thought picture: a bean plant heavy with pods beside a sunflower with hundreds of seeds.

pages.text: They tried a new rule. Not seeds for seeds, but space for space. Each of them had one flower pot. "Fill your pot with your seeds. Then swap pots."
pages.illustration_brief: Two identical clay pots; one filled with soil and beans, one with soil and sunflower seeds.
pages.audio_script: They tried a new rule. Not seeds for seeds, but space for space. Each of them had one flower pot. Fill your pot with your seeds. Then swap pots.
pages.image_alt: Two empty flower pots side by side, one for each child.

pages.text: Lan planted five beans in a ring. Nia planted three sunflower seeds in a triangle. They swapped pots, and neither of them counted anything at all.
pages.illustration_brief: Hands exchanging the two pots; a ring of five bean seeds and a triangle of three sunflower seeds visible in the soil.
pages.audio_script: Lan planted five beans in a ring. Nia planted three sunflower seeds in a triangle. They swapped pots, and neither of them counted anything at all.
pages.image_alt: Top view of two pots: five beans planted in a ring and three sunflower seeds in a triangle.

pages.text: Three weeks later, Lan's windowsill had three tall green stalks reaching for the glass. Nia's had five bean plants climbing a stick, already flowering white.
pages.illustration_brief: Split scene: Lan's window with three sunflower seedlings; Nia's window with beans twining up a stick.
pages.audio_script: Three weeks later, Lan's windowsill had three tall green stalks reaching for the glass. Nia's had five bean plants climbing a stick, already flowering white.
pages.image_alt: A windowsill with three tall sunflower stalks and another with five bean plants climbing a stick.

pages.text: In the summer, Nia brought Lan a handful of beans. Lan brought Nia a sunflower head as big as a plate. "Now that," said Nia, "is a fair swap."
pages.illustration_brief: Nia holding out a cupped handful of green beans; Lan holding a huge sunflower head; both delighted.
pages.audio_script: In the summer, Nia brought Lan a handful of beans. Lan brought Nia a sunflower head as big as a plate. Now that, said Nia, is a fair swap.
pages.image_alt: Nia hands Lan a handful of beans while Lan holds out a sunflower head as big as a plate.

quiz.prompt: Which girl had far fewer seeds?
quiz.explanation: Page 2: Lan tipped out forty beans; Nia's bag held only twelve sunflower seeds.

quiz.prompt: Why did both girls say the swap was not fair?

options.text: Each thought her own pile was worth more

quiz.explanation: Nia said twenty beans for six was not fair to her (page 2); Lan said the opposite (page 3). Each valued her own seeds more.

quiz.prompt: Why did the pot rule work better than counting seeds?

options.text: It swapped equal space instead of unequal seeds

quiz.explanation: One bean is not worth one sunflower seed (page 4), so they swapped equal pots instead (page 5).

quiz.prompt: What happened three weeks after the swap?
quiz.explanation: Page 7: three weeks later both windowsills had growing plants.

quiz.prompt: What is the big idea of this story?

options.text: Fair does not always mean the same number

quiz.explanation: Page 4 says one is not worth one; page 8 ends with a fair swap that was never about equal numbers.

quiz.prompt: Tell a grown-up how the swap went wrong and how Lan and Nia fixed it.
quiz.rubric: not yet: says they swapped seeds; with support: mentions unfair piles, with prompting; independent: counting seeds felt unfair to both, they swapped equal pots instead, and in summer traded the harvest
quiz.explanation: Explaining the shift from counting seeds to swapping pots shows the reasoning was followed.

items.text: Both say it is not fair.

prompts: Is a swap fair if both people are happy, even when the numbers are different?
What could you swap with a friend that is not the same thing?

off_screen_prompt: Offer a swap to someone at home: one thing of yours for one of theirs. Talk about whether it feels fair and why.
